wins.text: Record Q3 revenue of $9.2B, up 36% YoY, exceeding the high end of guidance; free cash flow more than tripled to a record $1.5B
Data center segment revenue hit a record $4.3B, up 22% YoY and 34% sequentially, driven by MI350 Series GPU ramp and 5th Gen EPYC Turin adoption
Client & gaming segment revenue surged 73% YoY to a record $4.0B; gaming revenue up 181% YoY to $1.3B on semi-custom and Radeon 9000 strength

Announced comprehensive multiyear agreement with OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs, with first gigawatt of MI450 Series starting in H2 2026, with potential to generate well over $100B in revenue over the next few years
Diluted EPS of $1.20, up 30% YoY; gross margin of 54%, up 40 bps YoY; client & gaming segment operating income expanded to 21% of revenue from 12% a year ago

risks.text: MI308 GPU shipments to China excluded from both Q3 actuals and Q4 guidance due to export licensing uncertainty, representing a meaningful revenue swing factor
Data center segment operating margin declined to 25% from 29% a year ago as aggressive R&D investment offsets revenue growth
Embedded segment revenue declined 8% YoY to $857M with operating margin compressing to 33% from 40% a year ago on lower revenue and end market mix
Power availability, supply chain tightness across memory, packaging and components flagged as potential gating factors for large-scale MI450/Helios deployments in 2026
Customer concentration risk flagged by analysts: OpenAI could represent a very large share of data center GPU revenue in 2027-2028, with AMD acknowledging the need to broaden its customer base

guidance_items.detail: Q4 2025 revenue guided to ~$9.6B +/- $300M, representing ~25% YoY growth and ~4% sequential growth; above Q3 actuals of $9.2B which already beat the high end of prior guidance
Q4 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~54.5%, up from 54.0% in Q3
Data center expected up double digits sequentially; embedded expected to return to growth (double-digit QoQ); client up sequentially
Gaming revenue expected down strong double digits sequentially in Q4 after holiday semi-custom pull-forward
Non-GAAP opex ~$2.8B; non-GAAP tax rate 13%; diluted share count ~1.65B; net interest/other expected to be a gain of ~$37M

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: MI308 China export license status and potential revenue upside if restrictions ease
Customer concentration risk around OpenAI potentially representing a disproportionate share of GPU revenue in 2027-2028
GPU useful life extension by CSPs and whether hyperscalers are sweating older-generation hardware longer than depreciation schedules suggest
